entries.reason: the backstop's third shape (2026-10-21): twenty-four hand-rolled spinners burned four cores each for four and a half hours, and the backstop knew only the house's own command line, so it left every one of them alone. So the backstop asks a shape it can NAME without owning it: an ORPHAN (parent 1) that has BURNED a core (CPU time over the floor and still growing) on a busy loop (the code a shell runs contains one) -- load_reap.burning_orphans. The lookup is a CANDIDATE list and nothing more: every candidate is read back and asked the four questions, and a live parent, a sleeper, a worker that finished, and a process that is not a shell are all left alone. The lookup and the kill are on ONE line so this rule sees them instead of a rewrite hiding them; pinned by tests/test_load_orphan_exemption.py, which is red if a question is dropped, if the floor is lowered, or if the exemption goes stale
